title: Prompts-The Power of After
coreMove: Anchor a new tiny behavior to the tail end of an existing routine by writing an 'After I ___, I will ___' recipe that fires automatically without reminders.

exampleSpecs.domain: a night-shift ICU nurse who keeps meaning to log a one-line gratitude before bed but never does
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who has tried phone reminders for a habit and watched themselves swipe them away
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a small daily reset that protects her sleep ever actually happens, or stays a someday plan for another six months
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse stops trying to remember and instead pins the gratitude line to the exact moment she sets her hospital badge on the dresser, because the badge-down already happens every shift

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school orchestra teacher trying to drink more water during the school day
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader whose new behavior keeps getting crowded out by an already-full schedule
exampleSpecs.stakes: chronic afternoon headaches that make the last two periods miserable for him and his students
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the before scene shows him buying a fancy water bottle and forgetting it; the after scene shows him taking three sips after he writes the warm-up tempo on the whiteboard, the one routine he never skips

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance bookkeeper at her kitchen table who wants to start a two-minute end-of-day shutdown ritual
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader whose work and home blur into one long evening
exampleSpecs.stakes: the difference between closing the laptop at 6 and still answering client emails at 10
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she discovers the anchor cannot be 'when I'm done working' because that moment never arrives; the real anchor is the click of the kettle she boils for tea at 5:55

exampleSpecs.domain: a recently divorced father of a seven-year-old trying to stretch his lower back so he can carry his kid without wincing
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who has confused 'morning' or 'evening' with an actual prompt
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether he can pick up his daughter at the school gate next week without the now-familiar shoulder spasm
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: in conversation with a friend, he realizes 'every morning' is not an anchor; the anchor becomes the moment after he hangs up his daughter's backpack on the hook by the door

exampleSpecs.domain: a graduate student in marine biology who wants to read one paragraph of a paper a day during a brutal qualifying-exam season
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who keeps choosing anchors that don't actually fit the new behavior's location, energy, or duration
exampleSpecs.stakes: falling another week behind on a literature review her advisor expects by Friday
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she walks back through three failed anchor choices and names the specific mismatch in each — wrong location, wrong energy level, wrong time of day — before landing on the anchor that fits

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional bakery manager who wants to praise one staff member specifically each shift
exampleSpecs.audience: a reader who treats anchors as optional scaffolding instead of the load-bearing piece
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether morale on her team recovers before two strong bakers quit for a competitor
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the reader is invited to imagine the same behavior with three candidate anchors — clocking in, the morning oven check, the first till count — and notice which one the behavior would actually hang on without effort
